attempts.label: DANDI:001708
attempts.paper_title: Multi-timescale Rhythmic Dynamics in Rostral Ventromedial Medulla Neurons
attempts.entry_title: Multi-timescale dynamics of RVM ON, OFF and NEUTRAL cells (Ashworth et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: The paper's central findings mostly hold in this data, but the width of the slow rhythm's spectral peaks and the heart-rate spectrum do not. ON and OFF responses around paw withdrawal, their sharper timing against withdrawal than heat onset, the five-minute spectral peaks and the periodic Gaussian process fits all reproduced. Peak widths came out near 90 s against the reported 17 s, and no reading of the described method gives the paper's figure. NEUTRAL cells also showed period minima like ON and OFF cells, and heart-rate spectral peaks at multiples of five minutes were not found. A minor Gaussian-CDF comparison also failed, and the comparison of fit quality between classes depended on which NEUTRAL data were used.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Ashworth, Martenson, Shi, De Preter, Heinricher and Mancini (bioRxiv 2025) on dandiset 001708, which holds single-unit recordings of 166 ON, OFF and NEUTRAL cells of the rat rostral ventromedial medulla, with heat onset, paw withdrawal, pinch and heart-beat times. It checks the cell and trial counts, the piecewise Bayesian models of the evoked ON and OFF responses and their timing, the slow (about five minute) spectral peaks and regularity of ongoing activity, the period scan and the Poisson Gaussian-process fits of ongoing firing, and the coherence with heart rate.

outcomes.statement: The evoked protocol recorded 104 cells in 53 animals (35 OFF, 45 ON, 24 NEUTRAL) and the ongoing protocol 62 cells in 30 animals (25 OFF, 25 ON, 12 NEUTRAL).
outcomes.source: Methods, Experiments, paragraph 4; Supplementary Table S11
outcomes.quote: total of 104 cells were recorded in 53 animals: 35 OFF-cells, ... 45 ON-cells, and 24 NEUTRAL-cells ... we recorded 62 cells in 30 ... animals: 25 OFF-cells, 25 ON-cells, and 12 NEUTRAL-cells
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), the Methods, the counts are exact. The evoked set ('evoked' and 'evoked/ongoing' files) has 104 cells (45 ON, 35 OFF, 24 NEUTRAL) in 53 animals and 53 files. The ongoing set has 62 cells (25 ON, 25 OFF, 12 NEUTRAL) in 30 animals and 48 files (12 rats with two sessions, 3 with three). Under reading (b), Table S11's three sets, the cells match (45/35/4, 0/0/20, 25/25/12) but the animals are 35, 18 and 30, not 35, 18 and 50. The archive lists 83 subjects, 77 male and 6 female, weighing 191 to 348 g, as the Methods say. No recording is deposited twice. No two units have the same spike count and first and last spike, no two files share heat-onset times, and identifiers and start times are unique.

outcomes.statement: The population PSTHs of Figure 1c pool 70 ON and 60 OFF cells, with 185 ON and 155 OFF trials aligned to withdrawal and 182 ON and 151 OFF trials aligned to heat onset, for windows that run to 150 s.
outcomes.source: Results, Canonical ON/OFF responses to noxious stimulation, paragraph 3; Figure 1c
outcomes.quote: shows peri-stimulus time histograms (PSTHs) for 70 ON ... cells and 60 OFF-cells, aligned to the time of paw withdrawal ... In total, 185 ON-cell and 155 OFF-cell trials ... were aligned to withdrawal, while 182 ON-cell and 151 OFF
outcomes.notes: The criterion's first reading (window from -30 s, pinches truncating windows) gives 180 ON and 151 OFF withdrawal-aligned trials and 177 and 147 heat-aligned trials, from 68 ON and 60 OFF cells (the dataset has 70 ON and 60 OFF units). All are within 10%. With pinches left out of the rule, as the code runs, the counts are exactly the paper's: 185, 155, 182 and 151. From -10 s they are 182, 153, 183 and 157 with pinches and 187, 157, 188 and 161 without. All are within 10%. With the window from -10 s and the criterion's 30 s before a withdrawal for the previous event (the verifier's point; reading (b) had used 10 s), the counts are 180, 151, 183 and 157 with pinches and 185, 155, 188 and 161 without, all within 10%.
deviations: The code builds its event list from events named "Keyboard", while its NWB loader renames pinches "keyboard" (Spike2Tools.get_tail_to_heat_lengths, data_loaders.rename_blocks_to_old_labels), so its trial rule never sees a pinch. Both rules are shown. Only the rule without pinches gives the paper's counts exactly.

outcomes.statement: For the models, windows from 10 s before to 100 s after the event gave 195 ON and 170 OFF trials aligned to withdrawal and 197 ON and 172 OFF trials aligned to heat onset; cells were not selected by pre-trial firing and every trial with a withdrawal was included.
outcomes.source: Results, Evoked ON/OFF activity unfolds over multiple timescales, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: This resulted in 195 ON-cell and ... 170 OFF-cell trials aligned to withdrawal, and 197 ON-cell ... and 172 OFF-cell trials aligned to heat onset
outcomes.notes: From -10 to +100 s, with pinches in the rule, there are 190 ON and 168 OFF withdrawal-aligned trials and 192 and 169 heat-aligned trials, from all 70 ON and 60 OFF cells. All are within 10%. Without pinches the counts are exactly the paper's: 195, 170, 197 and 172. The summed ON withdrawal counts without pinches begin 33, 26, 27, 26, 31, the first counts printed by the paper's notebook 18. Every model claim is fitted to both trial sets. On the set without pinches the ELPDs match the paper's notebooks to within one unit (ON double -7215.3 against -7215, ON null -11683.1 against -11683, OFF null -9237.3 against -9237, OFF linear -6264.8 against -6264.95, OFF double -6267.4 against -6267.36), so the paper's fits used that set.

outcomes.statement: NEUTRAL cells (n = 32; 69 withdrawal-aligned and 70 heat-aligned trials) show no modulation linked to heat onset or withdrawal.
outcomes.source: Results, Evoked ON/OFF activity unfolds over multiple timescales, paragraph 9; Supplementary Figure S3; Supplementary Table S11
outcomes.quote: trast, NEUTRAL-cells (n = 32; 69 withdrawal-aligned and ... 70 heat-aligned trials) exhibited no discernible modulation ... associated with either heat onset or withdrawal behavior
outcomes.notes: Re-run after a reader's answer (questions/001708.yaml) amended the criterion. It first took all NEUTRAL units of all files; it now takes the NEUTRAL units of the 'evoked/ongoing' and 'ongoing' files, which Table S11 shows to be the paper's n = 32 (20 + 12). The outcome before the answer was partially_reproduced, with measured 36, 76 and 77. Under the amended criterion there are 32 cells, with 67 withdrawal-aligned and 68 heat-aligned trials (window from -30 s or -10 s, with pinches), within tolerance of 32, 69 and 70. Without pinches, as the code runs, the counts are exactly 69 and 70. These 32 are the same units as those named "Neutral", the code's selection. NEUTRAL activity shows no change at either event under any reading. The test is spikes in the 2 s after the event against the 2 s before, Wilcoxon over trials. The median change is 0 Hz and p is 0.24 to 0.31 at withdrawal and 0.52 to 0.70 at heat onset. As a positive control, ON and OFF trials at withdrawal give p = 5e-15 and 2e-16. With all 36 NEUTRAL units, still reported, the counts are 36 cells and 76 to 79 withdrawal-aligned trials, outside tolerance, and 77 to 80 heat-aligned trials, and p is 0.14 to 0.23 at withdrawal and 0.49 to 0.65 at heat onset. The heat-aligned contrast has little power: it does not detect the ON and OFF modulation either (p 0.97 and 0.26 at heat onset), so the heat-aligned half of the test is weak.
deviations: Trials follow the criterion's rule with pinches truncating windows (as in fig1c-psth-counts). The code's rule never sees a pinch and gives the paper's 69 and 70 exactly; both are shown.

outcomes.statement: A null model with a constant mean spike count fits significantly worse than every piecewise model, for ON and for OFF cells, so both an evoked departure and a recovery are needed.
outcomes.source: Results, Evoked ON/OFF activity unfolds over multiple timescales, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure S8
outcomes.quote: Both null models clearly performed worse than either of the parametric fits.
outcomes.notes: With pinches (main), the constant-mean model's ELPD-LOO is -11704.9 for ON cells, against -7192.7 (double exponential) and -7438.9 (single). The differences are 4512 (dse 204) and 4266 (dse 193), z = 22. For OFF cells the null is -9241.4, and every piecewise model is above it by 2983 to 2988 (dse 122 to 123), z = 24. Without pinches the ON null is -11683.1 and the OFF null -9237.3, below every model by 4229 to 4468 and 2970 to 2973 (z = 22 and 24). Both readings of "significantly" hold under LOO and WAIC on both trial sets. The paper's notebooks print -11683 and -9237. Chains start at the highest of nine local maxima of the posterior (multi-start MAP, rvm.map_start), a sampler setting the paper does not give. Of the withdrawal-aligned fits, all but one converge (r_hat at most 1.007, bulk ESS at least 716, the four chains' mean log posteriors within 0.4 of each other); the erf model with linear recovery on the main trial set does not (r_hat 1.148, ESS 19) and converges at target_accept 0.95 (r_hat 1.004). In this execution the same model without pinches converges (r_hat 1.006), and so does its refit at target_accept 0.95 (1.003); in the verifier's round-2 execution it did not (r_hat 1.393, ESS 9). The heat-aligned fits converge with r_hat at most 1.008. The unconverged fit is also far above the null, so the outcome does not rest on it.

outcomes.statement: The switch from response to recovery comes 0.18 s before withdrawal for ON cells (97% HDI 0.27 to 0.095 s before) and 1.35 s after it for OFF cells (97% HDI 0.85 to 1.9 s after), so ON cells peak slightly before withdrawal while OFF cells keep falling after it.
outcomes.source: Results, Evoked ON/OFF activity unfolds over multiple timescales, paragraph 3; Figure 2g and 2i
outcomes.quote: differed for ON- and OFF-cells (Figure 2g) ... 0.18 s before withdrawal (97% HDI: 0.27–0.095 s before), and ... switch = 1.35 s after withdrawal (97% HDI: 0.85–1.9 s af ... Thus ON-cells peak slightly before withdrawal, while ... OFF-cells enter a brief post-withdrawal depression

statistics.about: OFF-cell switch time, linear plus exponential model

outcomes.notes: With the Methods' priors (k, k2 half-normal, the criterion's main reading) and pinches, the ON switch time is -0.191 s (97% HDI -0.275 to -0.105) and the OFF one 1.331 s (0.844 to 1.894), both inside the paper's HDIs, ON below 0 and OFF above. Without pinches they are -0.184 s and 1.312 s. With the code's priors on log k and log k2 the OFF times are 1.369 and 1.336 s. Every fit converges (r_hat at most 1.006, no divergence in the OFF fits, chains' mean log posteriors within 0.4). From the default start the Methods-prior OFF fit gives -0.636 s and does not converge (r_hat 1.69, three chains in the lower mode, 1121 divergences); in the verifier's round-2 execution the same fit gave 0.198 s (r_hat 1.75, two chains in the lower mode, 78 divergences), since the draws differ between machines.
deviations: Chains start at the highest of nine local maxima of the posterior found by pymc.find_MAP from switch times spread over the prior (rvm.map_start). The paper does not say how its chains were started. Started at the model's default point, as the code starts them, the OFF fit with the Methods' priors has three chains in a mode whose mean log posterior is about 240 lower (-6558 against -6320; 1121 divergences, r_hat 1.69) and does not converge in the execution recorded here. Draws differ between machines at the same seeds: in the verifier's round-2 execution two chains stayed there (r_hat 1.75, 78 divergences, t_switch 0.198 s). The start changes no method of the paper: it only keeps chains out of a mode whose posterior mass is negligible.

outcomes.statement: ON-cell recovery is better described by a double exponential, two decay timescales, than by a single exponential, which misses the sharp peak and the prolonged decay.
outcomes.source: Results, Evoked ON/OFF activity unfolds over multiple timescales, paragraph 4; Figure 2c, 2e and 2g
outcomes.quote: As shown in Figure 2c,g, ON-cell recovery was best captured ... by a double exponential model
outcomes.notes: With pinches the double exponential beats the single by 246.2 in ELPD (dse 22.7), under LOO and WAIC (-7192.7 against -7438.9). Without pinches it is 238.4 (dse 23.2; -7215.3 against -7453.7), the paper's 238 (dse 23). The single exponential's peak is 101 counts per bin against 127 for the double and 149 in the data, and its mean count over 5 to 20 s is 83.0 against 78.0 and 78.7 in the data.

Every loss history the code saved has 5000 steps, and the stored fits (combined_data.csv) have noise_prob 0.01. Matched cell by cell to the stored fits (by the null model's log likelihood, which agrees to a median relative difference of 0.0002 or less), the fits here agree with them (Spearman r 0.95 to 1.00 for period, outputscale, alpha and both pseudo-R2; median absolute difference of train pseudo-R2 0.0013 to 0.0024), so these are the settings of the paper's results. Expected log likelihoods use draws from each bin's marginal, where gpytorch draws jointly. The expectation is the same. The null model's uniform contamination runs over 0 to the cell's largest training count, as the code creates it (create_mean_model(T_max, max_count=train_y.max(), ...), printed in gp.ipynb); the criterion's "same likelihood" (0 to 200) is run as a variant.

findings.statement: The four NEUTRAL units of 'evoked' files (sub-rat-6, 7, 9 and 15) are named "NEUT", while the 32 others are named "Neutral". The paper's code selects NEUTRAL units by the exact name "Neutral" (Spike2Tools.spiketrain_iterator), so its NEUTRAL analyses leave these four out. This agrees with Figure S3, whose n = 32 Table S11 shows to be the NEUTRAL cells of the 'evoked/ongoing' and 'ongoing' files, but the label is spelt two ways for one class.

The code builds its trial-exclusion event list from an event named "Keyboard" (Spike2Tools.get_tail_to_heat_lengths), while its NWB loader renames the dataset's pinch events "keyboard" (data_loaders.rename_blocks_to_old_labels). Pinches therefore never truncate a trial window, although the Methods exclude trials truncated by the next event. The paper's trial counts (185, 155, 182, 151; 195, 170, 197, 172) are reproduced exactly only without pinches. With pinches they are 2 to 5% lower.

The EKG beat series contain 20546 inter-beat intervals under 50 ms (of 1105713), double detections at heart rates of about 400 bpm. They raise the mean heart rate per recording from 392.4 to 397.1 bpm. The 11 'evoked' files of sub-rat-25 to sub-rat-35 hold no EKG series.

The pinch events carry labels that are not described: 'ignore', ' ignore', 'l_hpaw_onset_approx', 'tail_release_post_pinch_slip', ear, tail and paw onsets and releases, some with a leading space. Nothing says which pinches were delivered, or what 'ignore' marks.

Table S11 gives 35, 18 and 50 animals for the Evoked, Evoked/Ongoing and Ongoing sets. The dataset has 35, 18 and 30 subjects, matching the Methods' 53 and 30 animals, and its Ongoing set has 48 files.

The text says a Gaussian CDF response fits OFF cells significantly worse than the sigmoid with either recovery model. The fits here, and the paper's own notebook 29, give the linear plus exponential erf model a slightly higher ELPD than the sigmoid model (here, on converged fits, by 0.42, dse 1.79, with pinches and by 0.88, dse 1.76, without).

Question for the authors. The Methods give the OFF priors as k, k2 ~ N(0, 1); the code places N(0, 1) on log k and log k2. Both reproduce Table S7 here once the chains start at the posterior's main mode. How were the chains started? From the default start, as the code samples, chains of the Methods-prior fit stay in a local mode about 240 log-posterior units lower (r_hat 1.69), and the result then depends on the machine's random stream.

Question for the authors. How were the spectral FWHMs (16.92 and 16.12 s) measured and converted to seconds? The peaks are reproduced exactly, but widths at half height of the per-cell or class-mean spectra give 84 to 106 s. The code's peak_widths call uses the index within the masked band, which measures the width about ten bins from the peak and gives 8 to 10 s. The supplement's rat-level bootstrap gives 58 to 98 s.

Question for the authors. The Gaussian-process settings differ between the Methods (200 inducing points, p_noise 0.001), the code (100 inducing points, p_noise fixed at 0.01, params.json 10000 iterations) and the saved fits (5000 iterations, noise_prob 0.01). The code's settings at 5000 iterations match the stored per-cell fits (Spearman r 0.95 to 1.00). Which settings produced the reported results? The code's null model also uses a different contamination range (0 to the cell's largest count) from the periodic model's (0 to 200).

Four ON cells in two files (sub-rat-70 ses-1, sub-rat-72 ses-1) have 228.6 and 226.5 s between the preceding heat onset and the start of their 1500 s ongoing segment, under the Methods' stated minimum buffer of 230 s.

The code samples the piecewise models from PyMC's default start. For the OFF linear plus exponential model with the Methods' priors, chains started there stay in a local mode whose log posterior is about 240 below the main one, and the fit does not converge; with the code's log-k priors some chains do so on some machines. The paper's numbers are those of the main mode.

The code's null Gaussian process (create_mean_model) takes its uniform contamination over 0 to the cell's largest training count, while the periodic model's runs over 0 to 200, so the pseudo-R2 compares two likelihoods. With the same range for both, the training pseudo-R2 medians rise by about 0.004.

The Methods say the full recording period of every NEUTRAL cell was used for the Gaussian-process fits (Data processing, paragraph 2), but the code's stored fits (combined_data.csv) of the 12 NEUTRAL cells of the ongoing files match fits on the code's 1500 s segments (median relative difference of the null log likelihoods 0.0003) and not fits on their whole recordings (1.28). Which input is used decides whether the training pseudo-R2 differs between classes (Kruskal-Wallis p 0.098 on segments, 0.034 on whole recordings).

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The handover of the author-answers run (executed notebooks evoked, ongoing and gp with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, re-run on the verifier's machine), the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier tested trial_times, times_on, times_off and spike_psd on synthetic inputs. Report in transcripts/001708/verifier-1-report.md. Its outcomes disagree with the record on five claims, all resting on OFF fits that did not converge on its machine.

disagreements.reason: The heat-aligned t_switch HDIs lie wholly after the withdrawal-aligned ones for ON and OFF (cell 40). The second part, tables3-s7-withdrawal-steeper, is only partial.

Linear+exp is 133-190 ELPD below the double exponential (cell 27). Both linear fits compared are unconverged (p_loo 117-138, WAIC warnings), and no converged linear fit was compared with the double exponential. The verdict rests on invalid fits.

The ON 90% rise (-0.250 s) is inside. The OFF 90% fall is outside under the main fit and inside under log-k. In both, the OFF HDI (-0.535 to 0.18) overlaps the ON HDI (cell 35). This uses unconverged OFF fits only.
ON 50% (16.9 s) and 90% (224 s) are inside. OFF 50% (35.0 / 27.1 s) and 90% (86.9 / 85.3 s) are outside (cell 36), from unconverged OFF fits only.

ON: the heat-aligned tau_pre is 1.309 s (inside) and the HDIs are disjoint. OFF: the heat-aligned k is 1.741 (inside), but the withdrawal HDI from the unconverged fit overlaps it (cell 39). The converged withdrawal fit (2.271-3.488, cell 29) and the converged heat fit (1.448-2.061) would be disjoint, but they use different trial sets.

entries.name: ashworth-2025
entries.title: Multi-timescale dynamics of RVM ON, OFF and NEUTRAL cells (Ashworth et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Ashworth, Martenson, Shi, De Preter, Heinricher and Mancini (bioRxiv 2025) on dandiset 001708, which holds single-unit recordings of 166 ON, OFF and NEUTRAL cells of the rat rostral ventromedial medulla, with heat onset, paw withdrawal, pinch and heart-beat times. It checks the cell and trial counts, the piecewise Bayesian models of the evoked ON and OFF responses and their timing, the slow (about five minute) spectral peaks and regularity of ongoing activity, the period scan and the Poisson Gaussian-process fits of ongoing firing, and the coherence with heart rate.
